https://www.dw.com/en/cuba-suffers-yet-a.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IABt Cuba has suffered several recent blackouts like this one on July 14 Image: REUTERS Advertisement Cuba 's state-owned grid operator said the island's power system collapsed late on Sunday, the latest in a series of rolling power cuts caused by aging infrastructure and a US energy embargo . The outage comes on the heels of three nationwide power outages last month. Cuba faces most severe energy crisis in decades To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video What do we know about Cuba's latest blackout? The state-run utility UNE said there was a "total disconnection" of the national electricity system, which means the entire country of 10 million people, including the capital, Havana, has been plunged into darkness. The Ministry of Energy said that protocols to reactivate the grid were underway. The series of outages afflicting the island in recent times have also affected water supplies and cooling systems, making normal life extremely difficult. Normal life on Cuba has been made almost impossible by the outages (photo from July 14) Image: picture alliance / ZUMAPRESS.com Cuba, which relies largely on aging oil-fired power plants, lost access to fuel from its previous primary supplier, Venezuela, after US President Donald Trump imposed an oil blockade following Washington's ouster and capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro on January 3 . Imports from Mexico , which subsequently became Cuba's key supplier of oil, have also ceased under US pressure. Supplies brought by a single Russian tanker in March with Washington's authorization have been exhausted. Cuba has also been under a broader US embargo for decades. Why the US won't leave Cuba alone To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Stepped-up US campaign against Cuba Cuba is also facing other pressure from the US, including ramped-up sanctions against Cuban state-owned businesses imposed by the Trump administration. These have led to a number of foreign companies suspending their operations in the island. Washington has also indicted former President Raul Castro over the downing of two civilian planes 30 years ago, in which three US citizens and a US resident died. The US redesignated the communist island as a "state sponsor of terrorism" for a third time in 2025, shortly after former President Joe Biden moved to have it deleted from the list. https://hungarytoday.hu/far-left-academi.text: Far-Left Academic Anna Unger to Head Controversial State Asset Recovery Office The National Assembly’s Committee on Justice and Constitutional Affairs has nominated Anna Unger to serve as chair of the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH). Six of the committee’s twelve members voted in favor of her. During her confirmation hearing, university professor Anna Unger said she envisions an agency with 150 employees. The political scientist, who regularly appears on the globalist radio broadcaster Free Europe and the far-left YouTube channel Partizán , was frequently featured in online media in the run-up to the election. Unger also said that she believes there would be no final court rulings in the cases brought by the agency under her leadership during its first six years. She also noted that she is not a friendly person and would not allow politicians to interfere with her work. Anna Unger will be elected by Parliament for a six-year term, with a monthly salary equivalent to more than €13,000. Anna Unger during her hearing before the National Assembly’s Committee on Justice and Constitutional Affairs on August 25, 2026. Photo: MTI/Balogh Zoltán The first reactions to Anna Unger’s nomination are now coming in. The TISZA-ÁVO will, true to the intentions of its creators, become a political cudgel—and a joke, albeit a rather crude one,” wrote Bertalan Havasi, FIDESZ’s communications director. The term “TISZA-ÁVO” is a political reference to the ÁVO, the communist-era Hungarian state security and secret police organization. The opposition members of the committee did not attend the meeting. On Thursday, FIDESZ and KDNP politicians also criticized the candidate for the NVVH chairmanship in comments to journalists at Parliament. Péter Takács (FIDESZ), responding to a question, said they had managed to “select the most disastrous candidate.” He believes it “says a lot” about the candidate’s suitability that not even all of the TISZA lawmakers on the committee voted for her. He criticized the candidate for having neither a legal nor an administrative background, but instead being a political scientist. Takács accused Unger of being “capable of hating with revolutionary zeal” and of having “called two and a half million voters brainwashed.” Csaba Latorcai, executive deputy president of the Christian Democratic People’s Party (KDNP), made his position clear to journalists: Anna Unger, who has been nominated to chair the office, is just like the NVVH itself. An organization built from the ground up for dictatorial persecution—the ÁVO of the present day,” he said. Gábor Török, a political analyst, wrote the following about the candidate: “She is a theoretical expert who is far removed from the practical aspects of the subject and who—as in the past—still fundamentally believes today that, before 2026, a dictatorship (an authoritarian system) existed in the country, and whose primary political objective is to prevent its return.” As for Anna Unger’s “democratic outlook,” it is worth quoting one of her statements from an opinion piece published after TISZA’s election victory: “Hungarian voters, in unprecedented numbers—nearly 3.4 million—placed their trust in a change of system and consciously gave up political pluralism in doing so. (…) In what many consider the country’s last great peaceful attempt, the country freed itself from an authoritarian system and reclaimed itself.” Three civil society organizations are set to advise TISZA officials in selecting the new leadership.
